question.problem:
Find the value of the constant $b$ that make the function $g(x)$ below continuous at $x=1.$

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}x-2, & x\le 1 \\ {b}^{2}+2xb, & x>1\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=1,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}g(x) & =g(1) \\  & =1-2 \\  & =-1,\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}({b}^{2}+2xb) \\  & ={b}^{2}+2(1)b \\  & ={b}^{2}+2b.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=1,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}g(x) \\ -1 & ={b}^{2}+2b \\ {b}^{2}+2b+1 & =0 \\ (b+1)^{2} & =0 \\ \sqrt{(b+1)^{2}} & =\sqrt{0} \\ |b+1| & =0 \\ b & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$ for $b=-1.$
